keyFindings.description: withinContext bounds store.Registry's context-less KV calls from inside the HTTP package; that duplicates session.SessionRegistry.Refresh's pattern at the wrong layer. Through senderStamp (api.go:353) it starts a goroutine, a channel and a timer on every send and publish that has a source_session, even when Registry.Get answers from its cache. Move the bound into store.Registry as ctx-taking reads (cache-first Get, RoleClaim, ReleaseExpiredRoleClaim), so a cache hit never leaves the caller's goroutine.

listenerDeliveryHandlerConfigs returns three copies of one value, and TestListenerDeliveryHandlersShareOneDeferralSet asserts the copies share a pointer, which they do by construction. A fresh set passed to main's rebind would leave it green. Revert to the one deliveryConfig value and delete the type and the test (or test behaviour across two handlers). Thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6wHB8w; my item 7b asked for this.

TestARoleLookupWhoseStoreDoesNotAnswerIsRefusedAsTheBusNotAnswering repeats the lookup/* subtests of TestARoleResolutionWhoseStoreCallDoesNotAnswerAnswersInsideTheBudget: same stalledRoleKV rig, same two cases, same assertions, minus the lower time bound. That costs 8 s per run. Keep one.

roleGetHandler (and the publish route's resolution path) answers every error other than the race through writeBusUnavailable, so a store error that is not a timeout, such as 'role claim has no holder' from internal/store/kv.go's decode check, comes back as 503 'the message bus did not answer' with Retry-After: 1. That label is false, and a retry cannot fix the error. The handler comment says any other failure is a call that did not answer. Give the store's malformed-record errors a sentinel and answer them as 500 without Retry-After, on both role routes.

publishCoreTo reads ctx twice and carries about 25 lines of comment because publishConfirmed takes a deadline, not a ctx. Pass ctx to publishConfirmed and check ctx.Err() immediately before publish; RequestCoreTo already holds a ctx.

unplaceableAgentDelivery finalizes in one arm and returns a bool so that its caller finalizes the other arm; the fallthrough is always finalize(false). Finalize in both arms and drop the bool and its contract comment.
